card_title: When He Called, They Did Not Answer
description: God calls and calls. But there is a point where the ignoring itself becomes the judgment. Isaiah shows both sides of God almost verse by verse.
excerpt: Reading Isaiah, you feel the two sides of God almost verse by verse. One moment He is inviting. The next moment He is warning. Both are Him. That is not a contradiction. It is who He is.
verse: "I will send them great trouble—all the things they feared. For when I called, they did not answer. When I spoke, they did not listen."
body_html:
Reading Isaiah, you feel the two sides of God almost verse by verse.

One moment He is inviting. Here I am, here I am. Ready to respond. Ready to be found. Longing for His people to come back to Him.

The next moment He is warning. I will send them great trouble. Because they did not answer. Because they did not listen.

Both are Him. And the whole book of Isaiah goes back and forth between the two like a rhythm. Judgment and invitation. Correction and comfort. Warning and welcome. Sometimes in the same chapter. Sometimes in the same verse.

That is not a contradiction. It is who He is.

He loves His people enough to keep calling them, keep speaking to them, keep waiting for them to turn. And He is holy enough that when they refuse over and over, real consequences follow. Both are real. Both flow from His character.

This verse is heavy. He is saying the things they were afraid of are going to come, because they refused to listen when He spoke. That is not God being harsh. That is God being honest. When people ignore His voice long enough, life without Him starts to look like exactly what they feared. Not because He is punishing them out of anger, but because a life apart from Him is what real trouble actually is.

Isaiah keeps showing us this. God is patient. God gives chance after chance. God calls and calls and calls. But there is also a point where the ignoring itself becomes the judgment. Where the trouble people were afraid of shows up simply because they refused the One who was offering to keep them from it.

I think it is easy to read a verse like this and only focus on the hard part. But held next to the invitation of the verse right before it, the picture is complete. God really is ready to respond. He really is ready to be found. And He really does grieve when people will not answer Him.

The choice is always ours.

He is calling. He is speaking. The question is whether we are listening.

Are you actually listening to what God is speaking to you, or are you hearing it and moving on with your day?
question: Are you actually listening to what God is speaking to you, or are you hearing it and moving on with your day?
